correctness.rationale: The exact 4x4 drift is Hurwitz for every permitted positive spring and friction by a strict mechanical-energy/LaSalle argument. Stationary Itô identities yield the explicit positive heat current, with independent flux definitions agreeing. At fixed G the reciprocal current has positive second derivative 2k²[p^{-3}+(1-p)^{-3}] and infinite endpoint barriers, proving the unique optimizer for every u,v,k,G>0. Its symmetry location and small/large G asymptotics follow from its exact critical equation. The package checker independently solved 10 covariance equations over rational parameters in eight exact cases and verified sample optimality; universal results are analytic, not inferred from those tests.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns the sharp unique split of a fixed total friction budget in the unequal-trap underdamped heat-transport dimer, not the known forward Langevin law. The full accessible primary texts were compared at the level of their equations and claims: arXiv:1301.4311 (2013) analyzes the overdamped two-bath dimer and its thermal current; Henkel (2021) states a spectral integral for arbitrary two-oscillator heat current including classical Ohmic limits, but not the fixed-budget unique allocator, its directional asymmetry, or the finite weak-contact large-budget limit. Barton (2015) considers identical oscillators in its accessible abstract and its full text was not available. Targeted exact-keyword web and semantic scientific-result searches returned no equivalent optimizer theorem among inspected results. This supports a qualified originality assessment, not proof of priority; the general 2021 current representation makes the present claim potentially derivable, but its constrained global optimization is an additional theorem.
residual_risks: The 2021 all-frequency forward heat-current integral covers this physical setup and could yield the current after additional integration; other researchers may already have optimized its classical two-Ohmic limit.
The 2015 Barton full text was not inspected, though its abstract is symmetric; a hidden generalization remains possible.
Indexed semantic and keyword queries cannot establish global priority, especially over older textbooks, theses, or non-indexed parameter-design papers.

value.rationale: The fixed total friction budget models a real thermal-contact allocation constraint. A complete unique optimum over both positive bath contacts, the direction of its strict asymmetry, and the singular high-budget saturation of the weaker optimal contact give an interpretable design classification. The asymptotic gain against equal allocation can be arbitrarily large across strongly mismatched spring families. These are not claims about mere correctness or isolated numerical constants; they resolve a natural full-parameter transport optimization problem. The classical, unit-mass, Markovian assumptions are explicit and narrow.
